name: Puzzle
summary: Riddles the world's own facts answer and locks opened by what was found out: a puzzle authored in the world or generated from its businesses, people, secrets, texts and keys, played by a director that remembers clues, answers, locks and keys while the knowledge base gives every verdict.

parameters.doc: wrong answers a riddle tolerates when the world's puzzle section names no limit (3); an authored limit, or null for never, wins

extensionPoints.signature: WorldIR.puzzle {riddles: [{id, relation, subject, prompt?, clues?}], locks: [{id, target, needs: [{kind: riddle|item|clue|lock, ref}], holds?}], finalLock?, maxAttempts?}
extensionPoints.doc: an authored puzzle; with no riddles one is generated from the world (src/puzzle/puzzle.ts)
the lid lifting: the engine plays it; the decision is already core's
read with readPuzzleBlock (src/puzzle/puzzle-save.ts), restored with PuzzleDirector.restore over the same world's definition

assistant.summary: src/puzzle/puzzle.ts builds the puzzle (puzzleForWorld: the world's authored section, else generated from it); PuzzleDirector (src/game-engine/logic/PuzzleDirector.ts) remembers each actor's clues, answers, opened locks and taken keys, and asks the KB every question; src/puzzle/puzzle-save.ts is the extensions.puzzle block. The engine draws the riddle prompt, the choices (puzzleChoices) and the lock, and plays open_container when told.
notes: Give the director evidence, not verdicts: findClue when a clue text is read, answer with the answer the player chose; whether it is right is puzzle_correct/2's.
Publish the definition (and puzzleWorldFacts when the KB is a slice) before the first question.
A save keeps only the director's state; build the puzzle again from the same world on load and restore into a fresh director.
Puzzle mini-games (catalog puzzle-minigames: riddle, combination, cipher, lockpick, sequence and word puzzles in a modal) are a later P9j slice: do not generate one from this pack.
doNot: Put a riddle's answer in the prompt or the binding: the answer is the world's fact.
Open a container a lock is on without unlock() saying so.
